title: A non-pth-power has nonzero differential over a finite coefficient subring
statement: Let $p$ be prime, $k$ a field of characteristic $p$, and $n,m\geq0$. Let $C$ be a domain equipped with a ring isomorphism $C\cong k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]][y_1,\ldots,y_m]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let $K$ be its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $M/K$ a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension] of characteristic $p$, with the $C$-algebra structure on $M$ induced through $K$. If $z\in M$ is not a $p$th power in $M$, then there is a subring $A\subset C$ such that $C$ is a finite $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and $\mathrm dz\ne0$ in $\Omega_{M/A}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], using the composite $A\hookrightarrow C\to M$.

proof.text: Infer CharP K p from the injective algebra map K -> M. Apply the constructed finite-subfield-family theorem to obtain an index type, actual subrings A_i of C, intermediate fields F_i of K over F_p, finiteness of C over A_i, image containment, containment of K^p, their intersection equality, and downward directedness.

Apply the finite-extension clause of FieldTheory.intersection_subfields_differentials to M/K and F_i. Set T_i to Subfield.closure(M^p union image(F_i)). Its intersection is M^p. It contains F_p because the prime field is perfect, so convert it to an intermediate field of M. The image and subfield closure are monotone; a common lower F_l therefore gives T_l contained in both T_i and T_j.

By D_eq_zero_iff_exists_pow_of_perfectField over F_p and the non-pth-power hypothesis, D(F_p,M,z) is nonzero. The differential-kernel clause of intersection_subfields_differentials for M and T_i says a differential mapping to zero for every i is zero. By contradiction obtain i for which its image is nonzero. KaehlerDifferential.map_D identifies that image with D(T_i,M,z).

Take A=A_i and retain the finiteness proof. The image of A_i in M lies in T_i by the image-containment clause for F_i and the scalar-tower algebra-map identity. Construct the ring homomorphism A_i -> T_i by this containment and its algebra structure. The resulting tower A_i -> T_i -> M has the same A_i -> M map as in the statement. If D(A_i,M,z) were zero, apply KaehlerDifferential.map A_i T_i M M; map_D and map_zero would force D(T_i,M,z)=0, a contradiction.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finite_subring_nonzero_differential
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
    (k : Type t) [Field k] [CharP k p] (n m : ℕ)
    (C : Type u) [CommRing C] [IsDomain C]
    (e : C ≃+* MvPolynomial (Fin m) (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) k))
    (K : Type v) [Field K] [Algebra C K] [IsFractionRing C K]
    (M : Type w) [Field M] [CharP M p] [Algebra C M]
    [Algebra K M] [IsScalarTower C K M] [FiniteDimensional K M]
    (z : M) (hz : ¬ ∃ x : M, x ^ p = z) :
    ∃ A : Subring C,
      letI : Algebra A M := ((algebraMap C M).comp A.subtype).toAlgebra
      Module.Finite A C ∧ D A M z ≠ 0
